Designing extensible domain models using the Open-Closed Principle (OCP) with polymorphic strategy injection in distributed systems represents a masteral-level topic because it moves beyond foundational object-oriented programming concepts such as inheritance and encapsulation and instead emphasizes architectural decision-making, scalability, and maintainability in real-world environments like microservices and distributed applications. At its core, OCP promotes the idea that software entities should be open for extension but closed for modification, encouraging developers to avoid altering stable, production-level code and instead extend functionality through well-designed abstractions. This principle is often violated in practice through rigid conditional logic or tightly coupled implementations, which can be refactored using polymorphism and interface-driven design.
